slots.operation: Distinguish carbon inputs from two immediate energy sources.
slots.prompt: Create one high-resolution landscape scientific teaching illustration for Alberta Biology 20. Title: "Two ways to build organic matter". White background, restrained forest-green headings, clear dark lettering, detailed but uncluttered textbook-style biological illustrations. Two side-by-side panels, both equally important. LEFT title "Photosynthetic producer": show a green algal cell in water with a clearly labelled sunlight arrow entering; a separate clearly labelled "Carbon dioxide: carbon input" arrow enters the cell; an output arrow leads to a simple labelled box "Organic matter". RIGHT title "Chemoautotrophic producer": show a scientifically schematic microbial cell beside a small dark hydrothermal-vent habitat inset, explicitly mark the inset "Example habitat"; a clearly labelled "Energy from inorganic chemical reactions" arrow enters the cell, separate from an arrow labelled "Carbon dioxide: carbon input"; an output arrow leads to a box "Organic matter". Give energy-input arrows amber dashed lines and carbon/matter arrows dark green solid lines, with a small exact legend: "Dashed amber: energy input" and "Solid green: carbon/matter". Do not draw an arrow from sunlight to carbon dioxide or suggest energy becomes carbon. Do not show an unbalanced chemical equation, sulfuric acid, giant animals making food themselves, or a universal pathway for all vent organisms. Neither panel should imply that respiration is absent. Bottom caption exactly: "Conceptual comparison, not a measured experiment. Other reactants and cellular steps are omitted." All arrows must have clear destinations, no crossed leaders, no invented numerical data, no decorative logos. Large legible text and generous separation for inline course reading. Generate the image, not a written description.
